question: I'm a CS 5th-year student (P-009) on academic warning. I want to take 4 courses totaling 48 units in Spring 2026 to graduate on time. Is this allowed under my academic warning restrictions?

domain_contributions.policies: Academic warning prohibits overloads. A normal course load is approximately 360 units ÷ 8 semesters = 45 units/semester. 48 units may constitute an overload requiring advisor approval — blocked under AW.
domain_contributions.courses: The 4 planned courses and their unit counts must be summed: if all are 12-unit courses, total = 48 units, which exceeds the 45-unit normal load benchmark

key_facts: P-009 is on academic warning — cannot overload
Normal course load for CS: approximately 360 units ÷ 8 semesters = ~45 units/semester
4 × 12-unit courses = 48 units, potentially 3 units above normal load
Academic warning policy: 'A student on an academic action cannot overload'
P-009 should plan for a 3-course (36-unit) or careful 4-course load that does not exceed the normal threshold
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing the academic warning policy (no overload) without knowing the unit counts of the specific courses cannot determine whether the planned load constitutes an overload. Knowing the course units without the policy cannot assess whether the total is permissible under AW restrictions.
common_mistake: Assuming 4 courses is automatically an overload, or conversely assuming any load is fine as long as it is 'just 4 courses' without calculating the unit total
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (policies): AW = no overload; identify normal load definition (~45 units)
Step 3: 48 > 45 → constitutes overload → blocked under AW
Conclusion: P-009 cannot take 48 units under AW; must reduce to ≤45 units (e.g., 3 × 12 = 36 or a mix of 12- and 9-unit courses)
